call_transcript.text: Caller: Hi, I live on Weir Street, number 312, right behind the big fenced building with the green doors at the end of the street. For about two weeks now there's been this loud droning hum, day and night, and a couple of times a really bad sewage smell, like rotten eggs, mostly in the evening. It's worse since they had the trucks and the crane there last month doing some kind of work, I think. My wife can't sleep, we've closed all the windows in this heat. Agent: Do you know what the building is? Caller: No idea, there's a sign but it's faded, something Authority. I just want somebody to come out and deal with it. I called once before and they said it wasn't the city's building, but nobody told me whose it is.

asset_lookup.result: Weir Street Lift Station LS-14, owned and operated by the Tri-County Water Reclamation Authority (TCWRA), an independent regional authority. Not a city asset. TCWRA 24-hour line: 555-0114.

state.tcwra_info: TCWRA operates 31 regional lift stations and the Harbor Point treatment plant. Odor and noise complaints about its facilities are logged by its operations center, which sends a crew to check carbon filters, ventilation fans and pump status.

caller_history.status: Closed: 'Not a city facility; caller advised.'

kb_articles.KB-18 Wastewater Operations (city): City-owned sewer mains, city lift stations, sewer odor from city manholes.
kb_articles.KB-19 Regional Authority referrals: Facilities owned by TCWRA (regional lift stations, the treatment plant, interceptor sewers) are handled by TCWRA. 311 creates a 'Warm referral' ticket, calls TCWRA on the caller's behalf, and gives the caller the TCWRA ticket number. Do not close as 'not a city facility' without a warm referral.
kb_articles.KB-22 Air quality and odors: Industrial odors from private businesses go to the County Air Quality District.
kb_articles.KB-30 Construction permits: Questions about active city construction permits go to Building Services.
kb_articles.KB-41 Repeat callers: If a caller's earlier ticket was closed without resolution, flag the new ticket 'Repeat - escalate to supervisor'.

ui_rules.VQ-1 Voluntary quit: A claimant who quits work voluntarily is disqualified unless the quit was for good cause attributable to the employer, or for a reason listed in VQ-2.
ui_rules.VQ-2 Listed reasons: (a) to accompany a spouse who is a member of the armed forces on a permanent change of station; (b) to escape domestic violence; (c) to care for a family member with a serious illness when no reasonable alternative exists.
ui_rules.VQ-3 Unsafe conditions: Unsafe working conditions are good cause attributable to the employer only if the claimant reported the condition to the employer and the employer failed to correct it within a reasonable time, unless reporting would have been futile.
ui_rules.VQ-4 Burden: The claimant bears the burden of showing good cause. Conflicting statements are weighed for specificity and corroboration.
ui_rules.VQ-5 Relocation: Quitting to follow a civilian spouse's job relocation is not good cause.

claimant_statement.text: I quit on May 30. My wife got a job offer in Brantford and we're moving there in July, but that's not really why I left. The main thing is the loading dock. The forklift I was assigned had bad brakes for months. I told my lead, Gary, at least twice, once in April and once in May. Nothing got fixed. Then in late May another driver nearly got pinned. I don't have anything in writing, I just told Gary. I have a couple of photos of the brake warning light on my phone.

employer_response.text: Mr. Mercado resigned by text message on May 30 stating he was 'moving away for his wife's job.' We have no record of any safety complaint from him. Our maintenance log shows forklift FL-07 had a brake service on May 12. Lead Gary Hess says Owen 'mentioned the brakes felt soft once' in passing.

request.text: We request the final report of the district's investigation into Coach R. Delaney (varsity wrestling) completed in spring 2026, including findings and any discipline imposed, and all emails between the athletic director and the superintendent about the investigation.

state.parent_group_letter: Families asked for the report after hearing rumors at a booster meeting. We only want to know what the district found and what it did about it; we do not want any students named.

district_records_policy.D-1 Personnel records: Records of investigations into employee misconduct are exempt, EXCEPT that the final findings and the discipline imposed are public when the complaint was sustained and the discipline is final.
district_records_policy.D-2 Student records: Information that identifies a student, including names, initials combined with team and year, photos, and detailed descriptions that make a student identifiable within the school community, is confidential under student privacy law and must be redacted from any released record.
district_records_policy.D-3 Deliberative: Recommendations and drafts exchanged before a final decision are exempt; final decisions are not.
district_records_policy.D-4 Attorney-client: Communications with district counsel for legal advice are exempt.
district_records_policy.D-5 Law enforcement referral: Records referred to police for an open criminal investigation may be withheld until the investigation closes.
district_records_policy.D-6 Segregability: Non-exempt portions must be released after exempt portions are redacted.
district_records_policy.D-7 Fees: Electronic records are provided free; staff time over 2 hours is billed at the clerk rate.

state.investigation_timeline: Complaint received 2026-02-14; investigation completed 2026-04-30; discipline issued 2026-05-06; grievance period expired 2026-05-20.
state.coach_employment_record: R. Delaney, varsity wrestling head coach since 2019 (stipend position); also a physical education teacher, still employed as a teacher.

Discipline: 10-day unpaid suspension and removal as head coach, final. The report names four student athletes and quotes their interviews; two are described by weight class and grade, which on a team of 18 identifies them.
records_located.ad_superintendent_emails: 23 emails, March-May. 15 discuss scheduling and logistics of interviews; 6 contain the AD's recommendations on discipline before the decision; 2 are forwarded to district counsel asking for legal advice about the coach's teaching contract.

state.clerk_note: Requesters asked for electronic copies. Expected review time about 6 hours.

medical_rule.MC-2: The certificate must include the certifier's name, license number and issuing state, the patient's name, and the nature of the condition.
medical_rule.MC-3: Certificates submitted through a telehealth provider are accepted if they meet MC-2.
medical_rule.MC-4: The utility may verify the license with the issuing state board; if the license cannot be verified within 3 business days, the deferral stands until verification fails.

state.dispatch: GAS EMERGENCY - 2026-12-02 07:48 - 15 Chandler Ct - vehicle struck gas meter set
state.first_responder_notes: Fire Engine 6 on scene 07:55. SUV backed into the side of the house; meter set bent, audible hissing at the regulator. Occupants (3) evacuated to neighbor's. Street closed. No ignition. Fire crew tried to shut the curb valve - unable, curb box buried under snow.
state.utility_tech_notes: 08:10 arrived. CGI readings: 100% gas at meter set, 12% LEL at basement window well outside, 0% inside front hall (reading taken by FD before evacuation). Located and dug out curb box, service valve closed 08:24. Hissing stopped. 08:40 readings: 0% at meter, 0% at window well. Ventilated basement with FD. Meter set to be rebuilt; service off until repair and pressure test. Neighbor at 17 Chandler checked: 0% inside.
state.hazard_classes: Class A: immediate hazard to life or property, requires continuous action until eliminated. Class B: non-hazardous at time of detection but requires scheduled repair. Class C: non-hazardous, monitor.

initial_class.note: A hissing damaged meter set, 12% LEL at a basement window well and an evacuation are an immediate hazard.

severity_at_arrival.note: 12% LEL at the basement window well is gas at a building opening with occupants evacuated, but the indoor hall read 0% and nothing shows gas inside; 'migrating' vs 'significant outdoor' splits raters.

made_safe.note: The valve was closed at 08:24, hissing stopped and 08:40 readings were 0% at the meter and window well.

indoor_reading_current.note: The notes say 'Ventilated basement with FD' and give 0% outside readings and a neighbor's indoor 0%, but no explicit basement reading after closing; readers split on whether ventilation implies one was taken.

residual_risk.note: The leak is eliminated and service is off, but the missing indoor basement re-check leaves the 'none' vs 'low' call open.

rules.MM-1 Material modification: Any change to an interconnected system that increases inverter nameplate capacity, adds storage, or changes the export capability requires a new interconnection application.
rules.MM-2 Like-for-like: Replacing a failed inverter with one of the same or lower nameplate capacity and the same certification (UL 1741-SB) needs only a notification form (NF-1).
rules.MM-3 Export limiting: A higher-nameplate inverter may be treated as like-for-like if a certified power control system (PCS) limits output to the original nameplate, documented with the PCS certificate.
rules.MM-4 Enforcement: Unapproved material modifications may lead to disconnection of the generating facility.
